newsitem.title: GERMANY: Stark-Germany to meet EMU in strict interpretation.
newsitem.headline: Stark-Germany to meet EMU in strict interpretation.

text.p: Juergen Stark, the state secretary in the German finance ministry, said on Monday he believed Germany would meet entry criteria for the single European currency under a strict and narrow interpretation.

"We will qualify in a strict and narrow interpretation of the criteria," Stark told journalists at a ceremony to change the presidency of the European Monetary Institute, forerunner to the planned European Central Bank.
Stark also said he agreed with the Bundesbank's view that sustainability would be important on determining initial members for the start of European currency union, set to begin on January 1, 1999.
"There is no difference of opinion between us and the Bundesbank and the importance of sustainability," he said.
Stark did not say that sustainability was more important than fulfilment of the criteria but said it was a factor that would be judged alongside numerical targets outlined in the Maastricht Treaty.
